title: Windows Staging bootstrap fetch housekeeping isolation

phases.objective: Keep the Windows local Staging bootstrap fetch isolated from repository auto-maintenance and submodule recursion while preserving exact-SHA, explicit exit-code, bounded retry, and fail-closed transport behavior.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The shared Staging Git transport performs fetch with housekeeping and submodule recursion disabled, accepts only a zero Git exit code, preserves exact origin/main SHA verification, and makes no Production or provider mutation.
steps: Invoke the shared Staging Git transport for the bootstrap fetch path.
Apply --no-auto-maintenance and --no-recurse-submodules only to fetch invocations.
Preserve the existing HTTP/protocol transport options, credential redaction, bounded retry policy, and explicit exit-code handling.
Continue to exact-SHA checkout and Staging preflight only after a successful fetch.
Require live Staging certification before this Staging-impacting change is treated as merge-ready.
assertions: Fetch invocations include --no-auto-maintenance and --no-recurse-submodules without weakening other Git command behavior.
A non-zero Git exit code remains fail-closed and retryable failures remain bounded by the existing attempt limit.
Exact origin/main and requested SHA verification remains required after transport success.
No GitHub token, credential payload, or local environment secret is read into evidence or printed.
No Docker, MariaDB, schema apply, migration, grant, provider, Hostinger, Cloudflare, Production deployment, Branch Protection, or Rulesets mutation is authorized by this change.

phases.objective: This Staging transport change grants no Production deployment, provider mutation, credential access, database mutation, or production_live authority.
blockers: Production effects require separate explicit authorization and independent governed evidence.
This PR is limited to local Windows Staging Git fetch transport behavior.
